findings.reason: Name and description say single-arm / unilateral vertical push; the flag says bilateral.
A single-arm press must be logged per side, not optionally.
Otis up is a weighted sit-up; iliopsoas is stored as a primary mover (hip flexion) alongside spinal flexion, so it spans two joints.
Prone forearm-supported chest lift held statically is a spinal-extension mobility position, not resistance training; gluteus_maximus is also stored as a primary mover.
Equipment is barbell/dumbbell and tracking is weight_reps/total_load; resistance comes from external gravity load, not bodyweight leverage.
Description is focus on stretching the trailing leg, tracking is time and biomechanics isometric_external: this is a loaded stretch, not a resistance set.
Description says isolation exercise performed standing to work the calves through plantar flexion - a calf raise - contradicting the mobility/time/isometric classification.
No external load exists; the only equipment is a mat and the assist is manual, so added_weight tracking cannot apply.
Assistance comes from a resistance band; there is no added weight to log.
A V-up lifts torso AND legs simultaneously; hip flexion is a major component, so it is not single-joint spinal flexion.
A neck harness carries free weight hanging on a strap; no cam machine is involved.
tracking_type is bodyweight_reps with no equipment linked, so a total_load input mode is contradictory.
Unloaded supine bridge with rotation: comparability depends on bodyweight, as stored for every other bodyweight_reps entry in the sample.
No external resistance exists; the load is the body's own lever arm, as stored for front_lever and tuck_front_lever_hold.

On a preacher bench the upper arm is fixed in front of the body and peak torque occurs near full elbow extension; brachialis in the same exercise is already stored as lengthened=high, so the biceps row contradicts it.
Description says dumbbells are pulled towards the chest while rotating the palms - a two-arm bent-over row.
Description includes alternating touching the toes with the opposite leg lift: hip flexion is part of the movement, so more than the spine moves.

Description states performing a vertical push while suspended from rings, but movement_pattern is horizontal_press primary / vertical_press secondary and the joint action is horizontal_adduction.
Muscle involvement inverted for a push-up variation: triceps_brachii_long is primary while pectoralis_major_sternal is demoted to secondary.

Joint action is shoulder flexion, the opposite of the sibling front_lever entry (shoulder extension), and latissimus_dorsi / teres_major - the prime movers of any front lever - are absent while deltoid_anterior is primary.
movement_pattern lists squat as secondary although the description specifies nearly straight legs, i.e. no meaningful knee flexion.

triceps_brachii_long is stored as a secondary mover of a fly, in which the elbow angle stays fixed; the stability ball required by the description is also missing from equipment.

Linked equipment is a straight barbell, which cannot be gripped with palms facing each other as the description requires; triceps_brachii_lateral is also primary while both pectoralis heads are only secondary.
